title: Surviving the Depression with steady work; lending a horn to Cyril August
summary: They say they always had work in the Depression, and the interviewer recalls lending a horn to the good player Cyril August.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: During the depression, all the other, he always give me awake. Another father used to give me awake. Then the guys used to come high on me. I was waiting every night. That's right.
I didn't feel nothing. I really didn't, what you call, really felt depression. No. No, because you had a job. I worked when nobody else did. That's right.
That's right. That's right. That's right.

That's lucky you got through depression like that. I used to, I used to halfway take care of one, one, one, great little now, something else we had. We never met season there. Yeah. We never, we never met season there. I used to even have to lend him a horn to go play with. Cyril August. That's right. That's right. He was good too, man. He had to lend him a horn to go play with. What's his name again? Cyril August.

Man, he's so... He was good. Yeah. He was there. He was real. Is he still around? No, he did. He was good. One of my tenders, he poured it and I was fixing to grab him but I looked at his wife and the kids and said, you know, mine. And he said, how do you know I had to get something for these kids? I said, sir, but you know, I'll let you go away from my place. I was waiting at the cotton club on Jefferson Highway. I said, I'll let you go away from my place. I said, yeah, but they had to have something and I didn't want my wife to know I didn't have it. Well, I'll go away. He was all right, you know. Yeah. He was good. He was good. He was good after play, boy.
